paper_metadata.title: A Hybrid Quantum-Classical Simulation Architecture for Catastrophe Tail Risk and Portfolio Optimization

experiments.description: Hybrid catastrophe tail-risk benchmark using quantum amplitude estimation on a synthetic Florida coastal hurricane portfolio, compared against classical Monte Carlo for 99.5th percentile VaR/TVaR estimation with error mitigation and a state-vector simulator with superconducting-noise profiles.

algorithm.variant: Quantum Amplitude Estimation (QAE) with zero-noise extrapolation and symmetry verification

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Parameterized loss distribution mapped to an 8-qubit register; non-linear tail-weighted amplitude encoding concentrates resolution around extreme percentiles.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate VaR and TVaR at the 99.5th percentile for a catastrophe loss distribution; tail-risk estimation error is minimized implicitly through QAE sampling and mitigation.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Classical constraint simulation with copula-based spatial dependence and VAR/ARIMA temporal dependence after quantum sampling; symmetry verification discards invalid samples.

problem_instance.description: Synthetic Florida coastal hurricane portfolio with physics-informed catastrophe calibration.

dataset_specification.description: Synthetic coastal hurricane portfolio; calibrated using HURDAT2-based stochastic tracks, Holland B wind-field parameterization, NWS-23 forward-speed asymmetry, HAZUS vulnerability functions, and a static gust conversion factor of approximately 1.05.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Raw exposure schedules, stochastic event catalogs, and wind speed footprints are transformed into a parameterized loss distribution; downscaling from sustained over-water wind speeds to over-land gust speeds uses land-use/land-cover roughness; tail-weighted amplitude encoding is applied.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Benchmark against classical Monte Carlo baseline; reported at the 99.5th percentile return period (1-in-200 years) with confidence intervals and estimator variance comparison.

hardware.device_name: state-vector simulator with superconducting-QPU-like noise profiles

noise_model.noise_type: superconducting quantum processing unit representative noise profiles
noise_model.mitigation_details: Circuit executed at a plurality of noise levels and extrapolated to the zero-noise limit; additional symmetry checks discard invalid samples.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Physics-informed calibration of hurricane hazard parameters; backend routing via a deterministic scoring function over precision, queue delay, and cost.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classical constraint simulation using copulas and time-series models; VaR/TVaR computation; confidence bands on exceedance curves; portfolio optimization via convex initialization and discrete local search.

speedup_claims.conditions: for quantum amplitude estimation in the idealized fault-tolerant setting
speedup_claims.caveats: Paper notes that full quadratic wall-clock speedup is not realized on NISQ hardware; reported gains are sample-efficiency claims.

speedup_claims.conditions: 99.5th percentile tail-risk estimation on a synthetic Florida coastal hurricane portfolio using 750 quantum shots versus 200 classical samples
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a sample-efficiency comparison, not a wall-clock runtime comparison.

speedup_claims.factor: approximately 53x constant-factor overhead relative to idealized QAE
speedup_claims.conditions: due to ZNE repetitions and shallow-circuit constraints on NISQ hardware
speedup_claims.caveats: Overhead is described as bridging theory and hardware realities, not as a speedup.

complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(1/sqrt(N)) convergence for Monte Carlo estimation
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: approximately 53x overhead relative to idealized QAE, due to ZNE repetitions and shallow-circuit constraints
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: approximately 7.5e2 quantum shots; idealized QAE cited as approximately 1,414 queries for pure quadratic speedup over 2.0e2 classical samples

experiments.description: Hybrid catastrophe tail-risk benchmark using a variational quantum eigensolver-style parameterized circuit for loss-distribution sampling on the same synthetic Florida coastal hurricane portfolio, with zero-noise extrapolation and symmetry verification on a state-vector simulator.

problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Classical constraint simulator imposes spatial dependence via copulas and temporal dependence via VAR/ARIMA after quantum sampling; symmetry verification filters invalid outputs.
